stories.headline: Catastrophic Glacial Flood Kills 939 People Along Nepal-Tibet Border
stories.body: Nepalese disaster authorities said a flood on the Nepal-Tibet border killed 939 people. Officials estimate that 3,925 people are missing across the area. That total includes 592 foreign nationals. Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah said rescuers saved 279 people from hydropower plant sites. Shah added that 11,379 people were saved across the country. Rescuers used explosives to blast into a hillside on Monday. They pumped air into the Trishuli-3A site to reach trapped workers. An international team with military personnel from China and Nepal is searching for trapped workers. Experts from India, Korea, and Australia joined the rescue team. In Chitwan district, rivers brought nearly 300 dead bodies to the banks. Local people carried out makeshift temporary burials. Chinese state media reported 16 dead and 546 missing in Tibet. Chinese authorities penalised people who speculated online that Tibet's casualties were higher. Nepalese researchers found an ice-rock avalanche triggered the August 26 flood. The avalanche travelled 22 kilometres in just over seven minutes. It moved at an average speed of 167 kilometres per hour. The flood affected 13 hydropower projects and one solar project. It knocked 431 megawatts of power generation capacity offline.

claims.text: Nepal's disaster management authority reported the death toll from the flood disaster on the Nepal-Tibet border reached 939.
Nepal's disaster management authority estimated 3,925 people are missing, including 592 foreign nationals.
Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah announced that 279 people had been rescued from hydropower plant sites.
Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah stated that a total of 11,379 people have been rescued so far across the country.
Rescuers used explosives to blast into the hillside and pumped air into the Trishuli-3A site to reach trapped workers on Monday.
An international rescue team comprising Chinese and Nepalese military personnel alongside experts from India, Korea, and Australia is searching for trapped workers.
In Chitwan district, river systems brought nearly 300 dead bodies to the banks, prompting makeshift temporary burials.
Chinese state media reported an official death toll of 16 in Tibet, with 546 people reported missing.
Chinese authorities imposed administrative penalties on individuals speculating online that casualty numbers in Tibet are higher than reported.
A study by Nepalese scientists found the August 26 flood was triggered by an ice-rock avalanche that travelled 22 kilometres to Rasuwagadhi in just over seven minutes at an average speed of 167 kmph.
Preliminary Nepal Electricity Authority data showed 13 hydropower projects and one solar project were affected, knocking 431 MW of generation capacity offline.

stories.headline: US and Iran Exchange Military Strikes Near Strait of Hormuz
stories.body:
US military forces launched strikes on Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on Sunday. The United States acted to prevent Iran from putting mines in the Strait of Hormuz. US President Donald Trump said that his country was going to hit Iran hard. Iranian state media said three people died in the US attack on Larak Island. The report added that several other people were wounded. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps gave a different casualty figure. The Revolutionary Guard said two people died on Larak Island. It said two other people were injured in the strike. Iran requires commercial tankers that pass Larak Island to undergo checks. Reports say Iran charges 2 million dollars for each vessel crossing.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards responded by launching ballistic missiles. They targeted two American military bases located in Jordan. The Revolutionary Guards claimed the missile strikes caused heavy damage to the bases. The United Arab Emirates foreign ministry reported military activity in the region. The ministry said UAE forces intercepted an Iranian drone over territorial waters. The UAE condemned the drone action as a dangerous escalation.

Iranian state television claimed that a supertanker hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz. US Central Command denied that claim. American military officials said no supertanker struck mines in the waterway.

The military conflict began on February 28, 2026. The United States and Israel started the conflict by launching wide-ranging strikes on Iran. Trump wrote a post on Truth Social about Kharg Island. Trump called Iran a failed nation. He claimed that the nation is dead. US Vice President JD Vance explained the social media post. Vance said Trump wanted to send a signal to Iran about Kharg Island. A US official confirmed that American forces did not hit Kharg Island overnight. Before the conflict started on February 28, Kharg Island handled about 90 percent of Iranian oil exports.

Iranian leaders called for peace during a summit in Kyrgyzstan. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian urged all sides to start a dialogue. Pezeshkian said that continuing the war helps neither Iran nor the wider region. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi also spoke on Iranian state television. Araghchi demanded that the United States return to its previous commitments.

claims.text: The United States carried out strikes on Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on Sunday to prevent Iran from placing mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
US President Donald Trump stated 'We're going to hit them hard' following renewed military exchanges with Iran.
Iranian state media reported three people were killed and several wounded in the US strike on Larak Island.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps stated two people were killed and two injured in the US strikes on Larak Island.
Iran demands commercial tankers passing Larak Island undergo checks and reportedly charges $2 million per crossing.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched ballistic missiles at two US bases in Jordan, claiming to inflict heavy damage.
The United Arab Emirates foreign ministry condemned an Iranian drone attack intercepted over its territorial waters as a dangerous escalation.
US Central Command denied claims by Iranian state TV that a supertanker struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
Kharg Island handled about 90 percent of Iran's oil exports before the conflict began on February 28.
The United States and Israel launched wide-ranging strikes against Iran on February 28, 2026.
US Vice President JD Vance said Donald Trump's social media post about Kharg Island was intended as a signal to Iran.
Donald Trump posted on Truth Social calling Iran a 'Failed Nation' and claiming 'IT IS DEAD!'.
A US official stated the American military did not strike Kharg Island during overnight operations.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian called for dialogue at a summit in Kyrgyzstan, stating that continuing the war is neither in Iran's nor the region's interest.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi demanded on Iranian state television that the US return to its previous commitments.

stories.headline: Lionel Messi Retires From International Soccer With Argentina
stories.body: Argentine soccer star Lionel Messi retired from international football on Monday, August 31, 2026. Messi ended his international career at age 39 after 21 years of national-team duty. He played 207 games for Argentina. Messi scored 125 goals for his country, making him Argentina's all-time top scorer. 21 of those goals came during World Cup matches. Messi won the FIFA World Cup in Qatar in 2022. He also won Copa America titles with Argentina in 2021 and 2024. In 2023, he won a record eighth Ballon d'Or award. Messi revealed that he wrote his retirement letter on July 21. That was two days after Argentina lost the 2026 World Cup final to Spain. He delayed publishing the letter because his father had health problems. In 2012, Messi set a record by scoring 91 goals in a calendar year. Forbes estimated Messi's total net worth at 1.1 billion dollars in 2026. Inter Miami owner Jorge Mas valued Messi's yearly pay between 70 million and 80 million dollars.

Lionel Messi retired from international football at age 39 after 21 years of national-team duty.
Lionel Messi made 207 appearances for Argentina and finished as the country's all-time top scorer with 125 goals, including 21 in World Cups.
Lionel Messi won the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar alongside Copa America titles in 2021 and 2024.
Lionel Messi won a record eighth Ballon d'Or in 2023 following his World Cup triumph in Qatar.
Lionel Messi revealed he drafted his retirement letter on July 21, two days after Argentina lost the 2026 World Cup final to Spain, but delayed publishing it due to his father's declining health.
In 2012, Lionel Messi set a calendar-year record by scoring 91 goals across club and international competitions.
Forbes estimates Lionel Messi's total net worth to be approximately $1.1 billion in 2026.
Inter Miami owner Jorge Mas valued Lionel Messi's yearly package with the club between $70 million and $80 million.

stories.headline: Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin Meet at SCO Summit in Kyrgyzstan
stories.body: Chinese President Xi Jinping met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. The two leaders spoke on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit. The meeting marked the 25th anniversary of the regional group. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov spoke about the meeting. Peskov said Xi and Putin mainly discussed economic relations. He said they touched on the Ukraine conflict only in passing. Xi said China wants to work with Russia to build an equal and orderly world. Putin suggested that the two countries cooperate on artificial intelligence and digital innovation. Putin offered to create a permanent visa-free system for visitors between the nations. He said China must decide if such an agreement is helpful. Putin said visa-free travel had already boosted tourism between Russia and China by 43 percent. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi also met Putin in Bishkek. Modi said India is willing to help solve the Ukraine conflict.

Vladimir Putin offered to establish a permanent visa-free regime with China if Beijing considers it beneficial.
Vladimir Putin noted that bilateral visa-free travel boosted tourist flows between Russia and China by 43 percent in the first half of the year.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with Vladimir Putin in Bishkek and expressed India's willingness to assist in resolving the Ukraine conflict.

stories.headline: Narendra Modi Meets Iranian and Russian Leaders at SCO Summit
stories.body:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on August 31, 2026. The leaders held talks on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit. This was the first top-level meeting between India and Iran since war started on Iran in February 2026. Prime Minister Modi urged Pezeshkian to work to ensure peace in West Asia. Modi asked Iran to protect freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. Pezeshkian blamed Israel and the United States for starting the conflict. Pezeshkian asked Modi to use India's many international contacts to help start talks. Pezeshkian said Iran remained committed to ceasefire agreements. He added that the American side failed to meet its promises. In July 2026, an Indian delegation went to Iran for the funeral of Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. The delegation included Bihar Governor Syed Ata Hasnain and Minister of State Pabitra Margherita.

Modi also held a bilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek. Modi told Putin that Russia should move away from endless war. Modi said Russia should work towards the end of war. Modi told Putin that India supports all efforts to end the war in Ukraine. The two leaders discussed attacks on merchant ships in the Black Sea. Those attacks killed at least five Indian seafarers. Modi and Putin rode together in Putin's limousine to the opening ceremony of the World Nomad Games. Putin said trade between Russia and India grew by 2.6 percent in the first half of 2026. Putin said almost 40,000 Indian students now study in Russia. He said that number grew seven times over the past decade. Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri spoke after the meeting. Misri said Modi and Putin discussed fixing the growing trade gap between the two countries.

Before the main summit, Modi met Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov. Modi also met Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan. Modi and Pashinyan discussed cooperation in defence, medicine, mining, education, trade, and culture. Modi attended the opening ceremony of the World Nomad Games in Kyrgyzstan. Formal talks between Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping did not take place in Bishkek. Officials moved those bilateral talks to the upcoming BRICS summit in India on September 12 and 13.

The August 31 meeting was the first top-level meeting between India and Iran since war broke out on Iran in February 2026.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged President Masoud Pezeshkian to ensure peace in West Asia and preserve freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

In July 2026, an Indian delegation including Bihar Governor Lt. Gen. Syed Ata Hasnain (retd.) and Minister of State Pabitra Margherita attended the funeral of slain Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi informed Russian President Vladimir Putin that India supports all efforts to end the war in Ukraine.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Vladimir Putin discussed Black Sea attacks on merchant vessels that killed at least five Indian seafarers.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin travelled together in Putin's limousine to the inaugural ceremony of the World Nomad Games.
Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that bilateral trade turnover between Russia and India grew by 2.6% in the first half of 2026.
Russian President Vladimir Putin noted that the number of Indian students studying in Russia reached almost 40,000 following a seven-fold increase over the past decade.
Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri stated after the bilateral meeting that Modi and Putin discussed addressing the growing trade imbalance between India and Russia.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi held bilateral meetings with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov and Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan ahead of the SCO summit in Bishkek.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Armenian PM Nikol Pashinyan discussed bilateral cooperation in defence, pharma, mining, education, economic, and cultural fields.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended the opening ceremony of the World Nomad Games in Kyrgyzstan.
Formal bilateral talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping were deferred to the upcoming BRICS summit in India on September 12-13.

stories.headline: India Rejects Hague Court Ruling on Indus Waters Treaty
stories.body: India rejected an interim ruling on the Indus Waters Treaty issued by a court in The Hague. India's Ministry of External Affairs called the Court of Arbitration illegally constituted. The Permanent Court of Arbitration ruled that the 1960 treaty remains fully in force. The court said India had no justification to suspend the agreement. The panel was chaired by Sean D. Murphy from the United States. The ruling ordered India to limit work on a hydroelectric plant in Jammu and Kashmir. Specifically, the court stopped India from concreting parts of the Ratle project dam wall. Pakistan petitioned the court in March 2026 to judge the status of the treaty. India suspended the treaty in April 2025 after a terror attack in Pahalgam killed 26 people. A proxy group of Lashkar-e-Taiba carried out that attack. The 1960 treaty gave India control over the eastern rivers Beas, Ravi, and Sutlej. It gave Pakistan control over the western rivers Indus, Chenab, and Jhelum. Since the suspension, India accelerated work on power projects like Ratle and Kishenganga. A World Bank expert will decide by July 2027 if Indian hydro projects follow the treaty.

claims.text: India's Ministry of External Affairs rejected an interim award on the Indus Waters Treaty issued by the Court of Arbitration in The Hague, calling the body illegally constituted.
The Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague stated that the Indus Waters Treaty remains fully in force and that India had no justification for suspending the pact.
The Court of Arbitration panel evaluating the Indus Waters Treaty dispute was chaired by Sean D. Murphy of the United States.
The Permanent Court of Arbitration ruled that India must limit work on a hydroelectric plant under construction in Jammu and Kashmir.
The Court of Arbitration prohibited India from concreting the Ratle project dam wall and power intake structure above specified levels until 90 days after the Neutral Expert's decision.
Pakistan petitioned the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague in March 2026 to determine the legal status of the Indus Waters Treaty.
India placed the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance following an April 22 terror attack in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir, which killed 26 people.
India suspended the Indus Waters Treaty in April 2025 as part of measures responding to a Pahalgam terror attack carried out by a proxy of Lashkar-e-Taiba.

Under the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty, water from the eastern rivers Beas, Ravi, and Sutlej was allocated to India, while water from the western rivers Indus, Chenab, and Jhelum was allocated to Pakistan.
Since suspending the treaty, India has accelerated work on several hydropower projects in Jammu and Kashmir, including the Ratle and Kishenganga projects.
The Court of Arbitration noted that a World Bank-appointed neutral expert will decide by July 2027 whether construction of Indian hydroelectric plants aligns with the Indus Waters Treaty.

stories.headline: Draft Voter Lists in India Delete Millions of Registered Names
stories.body: Electoral authorities removed 6.15 crore voter names from draft lists across 19 Indian states and territories. The deletions happened during phase three of the Special Intensive Revision. Out of 36.08 crore total voters in those areas, officials kept 29.93 crore names on the rolls. Delhi recorded the highest percentage of deletions at 32.78 percent. Delhi deleted 47.7 lakh names, dropping its electorate from 1.45 crore to 97.5 lakh. Maharashtra saw the largest absolute reduction, losing 2.06 crore voter names. That removed 21.1 percent of Maharashtra's previous voter base, leaving 7.7 crore voters. Karnataka recorded 1.07 crore voter deletions, which was the second highest total. Draft rolls also removed over 19 percent of voters in Karnataka, 16 percent in Haryana, and 10.8 percent in Andhra Pradesh. Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy wrote to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Shivakumar and Reddy raised serious concerns about the huge number of deleted voters. In March, the Supreme Court upheld the legality of the Special Intensive Revision process.

claims.text: Draft voter lists published under phase three of the Special Intensive Revision removed 6.15 crore names out of 36.08 crore electors across 16 states and 3 Union Territories.
Out of 36.08 crore electors on the rolls in the phase three revision areas, 29.93 crore names were retained in the draft rolls.
Delhi recorded the highest percentage of voter name deletions in the draft rolls at 32.78 percent.
Delhi's draft voter list deleted 47.7 lakh names, reducing the national capital's electorate by about 33 percent from 1.45 crore to 97.5 lakh.
Maharashtra saw the largest absolute reduction in voters, with 2.06 crore names removed from its draft electoral roll.
In Maharashtra, draft voter rolls retained 7.7 crore voters after 21.1 percent of the state's previous voter base was excluded.
Karnataka recorded 1.07 crore voter deletions in its draft electoral list, the second highest in absolute terms.
Draft rolls removed more than 19 percent of registered voters in Karnataka, 16 percent in Haryana, and 10.8 percent in Andhra Pradesh.
Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy wrote to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar raising concerns over massive voter deletions.
In March, the Supreme Court unanimously upheld the constitutional validity of the Election Commission of India's Special Intensive Revision process.
